(1) We introduce a deep reinforcement learning architecture, the embedded self-predictions (ESP) model that supports explaining why an RL agent prefers one action to another, and (2) We show that ESPs can be effectively learned in complex domains and support insightful explanations of learned policies.

we propose and develop a new method to explain the actions of a learned agent by contrasting the expected futures predicted for each action, and that this method is effective in three domains including a complex strategy video game.
